Industry News: Funny ha-ha or funny peculiar? Yesterday had plenty of both

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here’s a question: did last night’s Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match at St James’ Park show we can be the equal of the reigning Premier League champions?
  • At 16 minutes past six, after a miserably one-sided first half, you would have been embarking on mission impossible to find anyone saying “yes” among the 52,000+plus in the stadium or the millions watching on TV.
  • In a recent development, by the final whistle, blown nearly 10 minutes after the 90 by Chris Kavanagh, few would have replied “no”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here’s a question: did last night’s Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match at St James’ Park show we can be the equal of the reigning Premier League champions?

At 16 minutes past six, after a miserably one-sided first half, you would have been embarking on mission impossible to find anyone saying “yes” among the 52,000+plus in the stadium or the millions watching on TV.

In a recent development, by the final whistle, blown nearly 10 minutes after the 90 by Chris Kavanagh, few would have replied “no”. Such is football.

According to recent reports, let’s start at the beginning, or at least on the 12.30 Azuma train from King’s Cross to Newcastle. The LNER service was predictably packed with Gooners. Passengers in Carriage J were overwhelming confident of a one-nil or two-nil to the Arsenal, as they like to crow in north London.

Based on their team’s results this season, that was to be expected. They don’t score many and, apart from a blip near Brighton, they concede even fewer.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal are, in a word, efficient. I find them boring. The descriptions are not mutually exclusive. No way as the train rumbled into the magnificent Central Station about 32 minutes late was I looking forward to a feast of entertaining football.

According to recent reports, in dire need of a drink, I walked up Pink Lane with Big Nige, who had boarded the delayed train at York after it made an unscheduled stop south of the old Viking stronghold of Jorvik. Known as Eboracum in Roman times, btw.

Recent findings suggest that pink Lane was awash with happy Londoners. There are many, many reasons to be proud of Newcastle; one is the warm welcome the natives offer strangers (excluding Mackems, obviously. There have to be limits).

Which was why the mild hostility that greeted me in the Mosaic Tap was a substantial surprise. A young chap called Rob walked up to our table, where Paul and Gowa had already got in the drinks, and said: “You can’t wear that scarf in here.”.

His mate had apparently clocked me as a Gooner, having mistaken my half-and-half for an Arsenal favour.

A little bit of background. Remarked scarf was a souvenir from the Bayer Leverkusen v NUFC match. Not that I bought it on my visit to the BayArena shop a mere 11 months ago, when it would have cost £20. This one was acquired in October for a tenner in the NUFC pre-Christmas online sale, while present-buying for my daughter Jo and her family. The PIF need all the help they can get . . .

For all those who detest a half-and-half, that’s your prerogative. I view it as a reminder of a great trip, more useful than a match programme and less likely to be lost.

Recent findings suggest that rob swiftly realised his error, probably because I had slipped into my best am dram persona by screaming: “Look at the scarf! Look at it! You need to go to Specsavers, mate!”.

The faux outrage reduced poor Rob to a gibbering, hilariously apologetic wreck. “Sorry, sorry, I’m really sorry. It was my mate . . . What are you drinking, can I get you one, please?”.

Industry observers note that the free glass of malbec was much appreciated, thanks. Considering the prices at Mosaic, the scarf has probably paid for itself. Funny ha-ha, Rob.

According to recent reports, we played the “who would you select” game and all four of us agreed Gonzalez was not justifying his place. Starting Steur was a no-brainer, the back five picked themselves, based on the Fulham game, with Livramento available if needed to give us a second-half lift. The midfield and attack, apart from Steur and Barnes, were as clear as a peasouper.

According to recent reports, the big news at 4.15 was Bruno G starting for his new team. Who had expected that?

Recent findings suggest that there was just time for a quick one in Bar Loco, where I bumped into the legendary Tony Mallabar, before safely negotiating Turnstile 31 at the Leazes End. My seat in row MM was in line with the edge of the six-yard box, which gave a perfect view of the fourth goal, unfortunately.

In a recent development, the Booing of Bruno had been a hot topic. My opinion is that every opposition player should be relentlessly jeered, booed, abused and barracked (isn’t SJP on Barrack Road for a reason?) That’s what I recall, perhaps falsely, from substantial games in the Seventies . . .

Anyway, the Brazilian midfielder was booed from the warm-up until his replacement by Lewis-Skelly when we were leading 2-1. The effort of singling out our former captain probably backfired, because it distracted the more vocal supporters from doing the job of cheering their favourites.

Not that the players or the play gave reasons to be buoyant in the first half. Arsenal did what Arsenal do, using their 11 players against our outfield 10. Whenever Osula or Willock or Murphy or Barnes or Steur attempted to put pressure on Raya, he found the spare man whom our would-be presser had just left unmarked. Boring and efficient by Arsenal. Half-cocked and aimless by the Mags.

Recent findings suggest that in my opinion, Arsenal are no great shakes, whatever the title says. A great team have a top, top striker. They don’t. As they proved by managing only one effort on target before the interval. Hornicek didn’t have a prayer once Hall chested down a long ball and instantly lost possession near the edge of his box.

Our left-back is a wonderful footballer but, having rarely played as a defender in his youth at Chelsea, he is still learning some of the skills essential to be a watertight obstacle.

Sources indicate that murphy tried to catch Raya off his line with a speculative long-range effort and one other shot flew narrowly wide of Raya’s left post via a deflection off Barnes. There was almost nothing else of note in the first half as the champions biffed nearly every shot high, wide and ugly.

Burn and Thiaw stood reasonably firm, Dedic and Murphy seemed on different wavelengths, Steur harried Bruno G and Barnes revealed some unlikely aggression. Miley plugged away and Osula ran gamely but United lacked any sort of perceptible gameplan. We rarely managed to find a player in space. Worrying times.

Industry observers note that where was our next goal coming from, wondered my mate Dave at the interval. It had been a while at SJP.

According to recent reports, the answer came within four minutes of the restart, soon after the first of three stoppages caused by apparent injuries to Raya. More importantly, after Matthias Jaissle made a triple substitution.

Sources indicate that harvey Barnes smashed a shot low to the keeper’s right, ending a quick attack. Willock had pressured Odegaard into presenting the ball to Osula. An assist on the headless chicken’s credits, fitting reward for another tireless display.

This was when the match became funny peculiar. Miley man-marked Bruno, Arsenal misplaced passes, United won 50:50s, we found space to run with purpose. The gulf in monetary and player resources vanished as the Mags reverted to our best version of Howe-ball.

Only Hornicek of the summer 2026 signings was still on the pitch, Steur having been subbed.

According to recent reports, arsenal looked distinctly second-best. Raya went down again. A corner on our right from Hall was aimed beyond the far post, where the unstoppable Man from Blyth powered a header goalwards. In a frantic kerfuffle, a couple of blocks merely delayed the inevitable. Thiaw smashed it home and we were ahead.

Funny ha-ha and funny peculiar.

Around me in row MM, the earlier, almost incessant moans and grounds became voices of encouragement. Supporters who had failed to back their team in a dire first half were suddenly full of the joys of November . . .

Ramsey, Livramento and Elanga all caused Arsenal problems. For a few minutes, we battered them.

Industry observers note that then Raya collapsed for a third time. The long delay gave the champions a break they desperately needed.

In a recent development, whatever anyone else indicates, Jaissle and his men were right to keep pressing for a third. Arsenal were always going to fashion at least one good chance in the time remaining after we went ahead. To sit back with 28 minutes left, plus a lot of stoppage time, would have been professional suicide.

It has been revealed that my suspicion is that those who now bemoan our aggressive play would have whinged even more if the team had sat back. The match became attack and counter-attack. Arsenal, through Madueke doing a decent impression of the absent Saka, kept cutting onto his left foot. Hall, sometimes having to mark two opponents, let the right winger swerve inside and slam a low shot through two defenders and past Hornicek.

The keeper got two hands to the ball but could only push it into the Leazes End net.

In a recent development, havertz nearly produced what would have been a truly wonderful moment when his head diverted a late Hall corner beyond Kepa and against the crossbar. So near, yet so far.

Then Barnes capped what I reckon was his best game since Wembley 2025 by outstripping Rice on the left touchline and playing the ball perfectly to Ramsey on the edge of the 18-yard box.

Recent findings suggest that in the words of John Ando Anderson, just hit the bloody thing, man. Ramsey did. Sadly, though, instead of putting his laces through it, he tried to bend the ball into the postage stamp and it flew high and wide.

What a feather in Jaissle’s cap a win would have been. One point was good, three would have been great.

The late introduction of Wissa, who replaced Willock, was a failure. He contributed almost nothing, which has been the story all too often since his expensive arrival.

I would have thrown on Fernandez-Pardo as the game opened up. No team enjoy speedy opponents running hard at them and the Belgium international could have been the joker in Jaissle’s pack.

On the balance of play a draw was reasonable but this, like the Liverpool result, felt like two points dropped.

What is inarguable is the team’s willingness to battle for their mates, their manager and the Toon. Long may that continue.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.
  • Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break.
  • Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.

Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break. The Gunners have now gone nine games unbeaten in all competitions.

Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.

Although Arsenal have won the last three encounters with Newcastle, recent games at Tyneside have not gone entirely smoothly for Mikel Arteta. He will also have to make a few key decisions in the squad with players injured and a busy run of fixtures.

Industry observers note that bruno Guimaraes will certainly be a topic of discussion for this game. The midfielder joined Newcastle four-and-a-half years ago, playing an key role in the development of the side, before moving to Arsenal on a reported 75 million pound move in the summer.

Whilst he has struggled to make himself an automatic starter in Arteta’s side, he could have a bigger impact with the absence of Martin Zubimendi.

In a recent development, zubimendi is likely to be out for several weeks. Declan Rice should start, and Guimaraes is also likely to be involved, to form a double pivot.

It has been revealed that newcastle will try to play a gritty game to unsettle Arsenal. Despite Guimaraes’ knowledge of the opposition, he will have to assist the visitors to maintain control of the midfield battle.

Sources indicate that saliba is now back in contention after recovering from a back injury. The Frenchman has not played in the first team this season, but has made two appearances as he recovers. He played 45 minutes for the U21s.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba is in good shape and will begin to play more games, though he is unlikely to be in the starting line-up for the game against Newcastle.

Recent findings suggest that konsa should be in the starting line-up alongside Gabriel. Saliba could come on from the bench, as he looks to make his first competitive appearance of the season after the Champions League final last time out.

Sources indicate that saka is still unavailable due to quad trouble, whilst Dowman is suspended. Madueke should start on the right and Havertz will spearhead the attack.

Newcastle United: Predicted line-up not confirmed in the supplied team news.

Arsenal: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Arsenal absentees: Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman.

Saliba is available but is not expected to start.

Newcastle have leaked goals at home this season. However, with Madueke and Tzolis providing pace in wide areas, this should not worry Arsenal too much.

Nevertheless, this game should be challenging for the Gunners. Newcastle are dangerous in attack and can capitalise on errors quickly in possession.

Despite Arsenal’s solid defensive record, they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their 4 visits to St James’ Park.

Sources indicate that overall this should be a good watch with goals scored by both sides. However, Arsenal should be able to pick up some vital 3 points.

Predicted score: Newcastle United 2-3 Arsenal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just over one year ago, West Ham’s Finlay Herrick was stepping out on loan for Boreham Wood in the National League – the fifth tier of English football. A far cry from London Stadium yesterday as he replaced Mads Hermansen in goal and made his Championship debut, apparently hearing about his impending start just on the morning of the game.

And despite the first half concession from the corner, Herrick did a pretty fair job with excellent double saves later in the game and some assured glove work catching the ball – which had seemed like a lost art at times in the last couple of years.

Herrick after his unforgettable FA Cup penalty shootout debut last year.

In a recent development, this was a massive gamble by Scott Parker which could have backfired dreadfully. With no Areola, the temptation must have been to revert to Hermansen yet the Hammers’ head coach stuck with his instinct. After the first half goal concession, Parker must have wondered – briefly – whether he’d made a huge howler.

Sources indicate that has Herrick done enough to keep his place? It seems Parker is dead set on replacing Hermansen so until Alphonse Areola is ‘fit and ready’ then Herrick should be prepared for more pitch time. He certainly has the ambition:.

“I hope this is the start. I hope I’ve done myself justice and proved to the fans that I don’t just want to be third choice, I want to be playing, I want to get back to the Premier League and be part of that”. (whu/youtube).

Describing the competition amongst the trio of goal keepers, Herrick was quick to praise Hermansen for the encouragement and help he’s received recently, describing the three keepers as a team more than individuals fighting amongst themselves for the sole starting spot:.

“There’s one goal keeper shirt and there’s three of us – but we’re like a band of brothers and we always stick together, me Mads and Fonz- no matter what. “.

According to recent reports, difficult to believe Herrick is still only 20 – he seems to have been around West Ham’s fringes for ever- but he joined the academy at six years old and looks to have the talent to go all the way. From yesterday’s solid start, he didn’t let his manager or his team mates down and should feel rightly pretty proud of himself.

The question for Scott Parker is whether he continues between the sticks at Fratton Park on Tuesday night.

Call Me Crazy, But I’m Still Backing This West Ham Team – Here’s Why

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As I left the London Stadium to a chorus of boos, I found myself desperately searching for positives from a frustrating 1-1 draw against the league’s bottom club.
  • Industry observers note that the first was the performance of Alvarez.
  • It has been revealed that the second positive was that the statistics backed up what I’d watched unfold on the pitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As I left the London Stadium to a chorus of boos, I found myself desperately searching for positives from a frustrating 1-1 draw against the league’s bottom club.

Industry observers note that the first was the performance of Alvarez. Largely cast into the shadows through the stubbornness of our former manager, he grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck. He took control, lifted the crowd, and, above all, displayed the leadership qualities this team has lacked for much of the season.

It has been revealed that the second positive was that the statistics backed up what I’d watched unfold on the pitch. West Ham dominated possession with 79%, registered 30 shots, and recorded an xG of 3.13. The problem? Only four of those efforts were shots on target.

We gifted Preston their opening goal. It came from a calamitous mix-up, with Piroe’s flicked header looping backwards onto the crossbar before dropping kindly for Liam Lindsay to tap home from close range. It could be argued that Herrick should have been more commanding from the corner, but he made amends later with an excellent double save.

There were concerns that we wouldn’t pull one back, we did on the 60th minute, Mavropanos heading home his sixth goal in 15 league appearances this season.

Industry observers note that “Ifs” and “buts” don’t win football matches, and as Parker said afterwards: “The overall performance suggests we should win. The fine margins of football are, and the reality is, if Tomas Soucek scores that last-minute goal, it’s probably a different interview.”.

For me, I’m not going to be negative. We needed a win and we didn’t get the three points, but what I want to see now is the team build on the domination, the chance creation and the shot volume by going to Fratton Park on Tuesday and getting the job done. If we concede first there and deliver an abject performance, then and only then will there be more serious questions to ask.

Nick Woltemade was left out of the Juventus starting eleven on Sunday.

A Serie A home match against Venezia.

After a woeful goalless opening half Juventus were booed off the pitch.

Nick Woltemade introduced for the start of the second half and the rest is history.

Within 14 minutes Juventus had the game won.

Nick Woltemade scoring the opening goal within eight minutes of entering the pitch.

It was then 2-0 within 14 minutes as the Newcastle United loan star got the assist for Teun Koopmeiners.

Juan Cabal a third goal, before then Nick Woltemade passed up the chance of scoring his second when he handed the ball to fellow striker Randal Kolo Muani to score from the penalty spot.

A goalless first half shocker transformed into a thumping second half 4-0 Juventus triumph.

Supersub Nick Woltemade handed the man of the match trophy after the final whistle.

When Sports Dunia reported on the match. they waxed lyrical about the contribution of Nick Woltemade: ‘Came on and instantly changed the game. His close-range finish for the opener broke Venezia’s resistance and shifted all momentum. We noticed his intelligent movement between lines, dragging defenders out of shape. He also assisted Koopmeiners, showing composure in the box. From our perspective, a superb super-sub performance.’.

Nick Woltemade has still only started seven games in all competitions for Juventus but now has eight direct goal contributions, scoring five and getting three assists.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday was a bizarre and surreal experience at the London Stadium as we watched West Ham’s half-hearted attempts to beat a stubborn Preston North End side. Sure, the Hammers had 30 shots and an impressive 79% slice of the possession pie. But scratch below the surface and there are still big problems with Scott Parker’s team, some of which I suspect will not be sorted out until the January transfer window.

Despite West Ham’s impressive array of shots, passes and corners, I never truly felt that the team had the magic or the cutting edge to win the game. And as crazy as it sounds, considering we’d hit the post twice and had 14 corners, I don’t actually think we threatened enough. The Hammers lacked sparkle and magic, for sure.

Alvarez- first game back in claret and blue for a year and a half.

Edson Álvarez was an excellent addition to the team, but he is a defensive midfielder, and realistically, the defence was improved. Herrick made a bit of a blooper in goal for the opener, but I felt he redeemed himself with an excellent double save. By and large, West Ham restricted Preston’s chances, and so we should have done. After all, they’re the worst team in the division.

But our biggest problems came in attack. Edvin Austbø on the left wing flattered to deceive, cutting inside and shooting just off target at one point, but never really terrorising his marker, despite the fact that he had him on a yellow card. Joël Piroe did okay but fluffed his major chance when put through by Arne Engels.

As for the supply line, Divine Mukasa flitted in and out of the game and did not create anywhere near enough, given his deployment in the number 10 position. Jarrod Bowen was wide. I mean, very wide for so much of the game that he was probably on first-name terms with the linesman. But realistically, he was just out of the game for large parts of it. We’ll get into more detail on that later.

Sources indicate that overall, it was nowhere near enough quality. Sure, we had momentum. Sure, we had possession. But this did not look like a group of Premier League-standard players against the worst team in the division.

Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.

Industry observers note that evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness. The result left the Seasiders immediately above the League One relegation zone and followed a run of one win and six defeats in ten league games.

Blackpool’s social media team had earlier wished Evatt a happy 45th birthday with the pay-off line: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'.

Three hours later, Evatt was relieved of his duties, and the club began the search for their ninth manager in eight years.

Evatt’s contract was set to run until June 2028. He joined last October following his exit from Bolton Wanderers in January 2025.

Blackpool later thanked the 45-year-old for his efforts during his time with the club.

Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy 45th birthday.

Blackpool posted the birthday message just after 9am in the morning, with Evatt's sacking then confirmed at 4pm.

Former Crystal Palace chairman Simon Jordan famously claimed to have sacked Trevor Francis on his birthday back in 2003.

Francis' dismissal has become an often told tale, with Jordan writing sixteen years after the event that he had even offered to send the former England star a birthday card.

Recent reports have also involved the suggestion that Francis had mumbled 'but its my birthday' back to Jordan when he was given his marching orders.

Whether these events played out as told are unclear. But Crystal Palace officially revealed Francis' departure on April 18 in 2003, with his birthday falling a day later.

According to recent reports, 'I am totally committed to playing in the Premier League and I will ensure the newly introduced manager can achieve this aspiration,' Jordan wrote on Crystal Palace's website at the time. 'I would like to thank Trevor for all his hard work and would like to wish him the very best for the future.'.

In a recent development, jordan then turned on the players, adding: 'I'm not watching next year what I've had to watch this year. At times we've been a disgrace.

'I've asked the management staff to tell me who should go. They can see the players who are performing and those who are not and you will see in the summer, out they will go. The players will be told when it suits me. I care about them as much they care about me.'.

Francis had reportedly told his players in a parting shot: 'Well, lads, I've been sacked – have a good summer holiday.'.

Palace appointed Steve Kember as manager in the summer and despite Jordan's hopes of automatic promotion, rather than the play-offs, found themselves in a relegation battle in November.

Iain Dowie was appointed as manager the following month and guided Palace into the play-offs, with the Eagles triumphing in Cardiff to secure promotion to the top flight.

Steve Thompson will step in to take charge of the team against Wigan Athletic this weekend, his fourth spell as caretaker, alongside Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks.

During a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for Blackpool. In his six years at the club, he played a vital role in their rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

On arrival as a manager, he amassed 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 to lift them out of the relegation zone, although they lost ten and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again this season.

Taken in isolation yesterday’s team performance at London Stadium doesn’t look quite so poor: A draw against the bottom side who had just beaten promotion prospects Southampton symbolises everything good about this Championship: Predictable it is not.

It has been revealed that west Ham hit the wood work four times and on another day could easily have romped home. Trouble is, after the losses and draws of recent weeks a solitary point does nothing to halt the downward slide. It does seem a little early to start demanding change to Parker’s starting eleven – who as a unit were paying together for the first time yesterday.

Nuno was ‘the tinker man’ and you’d hope Scott Parker will persevere, despite criticism and articles today demanding the immediate axing of key players.

Piroe scored on his debut – surely it is a little early to consider discarding the striker who needs a run in Parker’s side.

Footballfancast.com is typical in calling for Joel Piroe to be dropped after his poor game:.

“The left-footed attacker delivered a dismal display in the centre-forward position and must be dropped by Parker ahead of the trip to Portsmouth in midweek”.

The real problem with that knee-jerk reaction is that there is, simply put, nobody else to fill that role: Castellanos was invisible yesterday and fluffed his one chance, a header at the far post that didn’t get within a yard of the target. Pablo is, to all intents and purposes, finished now that his benefactor Nuno has left and until January, the cupboard is bare unless Parker gambles all on one of the youngsters.

Piroe needs the same kind of run which Castellanos had in the team before discarding him: He’s already outscored the Argentine forward by 4 goals to 1 this season. Give him a break.

West Ham’s Answer Was There All Along – So Why Ignore It?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • At the risk of sounding like a scratched record, West Ham have an emergency, break-glass solution to breaking teams down.
  • What’s particularly puzzling is that I genuinely believe the best we’ve seen Bowen play in the last couple of years came during the second half against Cardiff City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United’s lack of cutting edge against Preston North End was concerning, but perhaps the most frustrating aspect of Saturday’s 1-1 draw was that Scott Parker already appears to have the answer to the Hammers’ creative problems.

At the risk of sounding like a scratched record, West Ham have an emergency, break-glass solution to breaking teams down. It’s called Jarrod Bowen, and I’m not entirely sure I’ve ever seen our captain play wider than he did at the London Stadium yesterday.

What’s particularly puzzling is that I genuinely believe the best we’ve seen Bowen play in the last couple of years came during the second half against Cardiff City. On that occasion, Parker was effectively handed a blueprint for getting the best out of West Ham’s most important player, yet we’ve barely seen it since.

During that extraordinary second-half comeback against Cardiff, Bowen was given a certain amount of freedom, perhaps encouraged by Parker or maybe he just took it upon himself to drift into the middle of the pitch and cause havoc.

Whatever the reason, he had a hand in all three West Ham goals, and the difference was remarkable.

For the first, he drifted into what might be regarded as the number 10 position and chipped a lovely ball over the Cardiff back line for Divine Mukasa to finish.

According to recent reports, the second was similar, with Bowen again creating the opening from a central position. His pass found Joël Piroe, whose flick released Arne Engels to score.

The third goal saw Bowen back in his more familiar position on the right-hand side, where he supplied a wonderful inswinging cross for Max Kilman to equalise.

Jarrod Bowen was given license to roam against Cardiff.

Recent findings suggest that but that only went to show quite how much freedom Bowen had. In essence, he was everywhere.

As a blueprint, Scott Parker couldn’t have been given a better gift on his first day in charge than discovering that West Ham’s best player could operate with devastating effect from a free role.

Indeed, I was so encouraged by what I saw that I subsequently wrote about how Scott Parker must restore West Ham’s most dangerous weapon following the defeat at Blackburn.

Because for a brief period against Cardiff, it looked as though we’d stumbled upon something rather special.

Therefore, I was a little underwhelmed that we didn’t see it repeated against Blackburn and very worried when we probably saw our captain more straightjacketed than ever against Preston North End.

If I could offer Parker one piece of encouragement or advice, it would be to get the best out of Bowen.

I’m quite sure our new head coach will improve the defence, and I think we saw signs of that yesterday, albeit against the league’s worst team.

But it can’t come at the expense of shackling our best player, who potentially could only be here for a few more months.

As I argued in my assessment of the Preston draw, West Ham had plenty of possession, shots and territory, but very little magic.

In a recent development, and that’s the really bloody annoying part. We have a player who can provide exactly that, but we’re asking him to operate in a way which makes life considerably easier for the opposition.

Industry observers note that I know one thing. If I was head coach of an opposition Championship team and I saw Jarrod Bowen shackled to the right wing, I’d breathe a huge sigh of relief.

Because West Ham get one shot at this.

In a recent development, if we don’t succeed in getting promotion, Bowen could leave for a pittance of £15m. That’s the release clause in the revised contract he agreed following relegation.

We do know that Bowen flew to Prague to meet Daniel Křetínský before pledging to remain at West Ham for another season, as he explained in his interview with Sky Sports.

And I’m now very fearful that we are going to waste what should really be something of a cheat code for the division.

Bowen is comfortably our best attacking player, and we’ve already seen how devastating he can be when allowed to roam. Yet rather than building upon that discovery, Parker appears to have returned him to a position where he’s easier to mark and less able to influence the game.

I wish it weren’t so, but I’ve now come to the conclusion that the second half against Cardiff was a pure accident rather than a window into what we could begin to see from Scott Parker as he got his teeth into the West Ham job.

But decisions like that could well make the difference between automatic promotion and a play-off place, if we’re lucky.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that senior Correspondent AUTHORITY Senior football correspondent and podcast host with specialist knowledge across the Premier League and SPFL. FOCUS Transfer news, breaking stories, and behind-the-scenes insight across Arsenal, Liverpool, Celtic, and Manchester United. THE INSIGHT Callum utilises a network of club and industry contacts across the Premier League and SPFL to deliver verified, high-speed reporting. He provides the depth behind the headlines — from breaking transfer news to behind-the-scenes developments — ensuring fans get the full story as it happens.

Peter Bankes had a strong outing as Hull City secured a huge 2-0 win against Brighton on 22 November.

The 44-year-old took charge of the 2pm kick-off at the MKM Stadium, which was broadcast live on Sky Sports, in what was an impotant clash at both ends of the table.

The referee had one major decision to make and showed Joao Costinha a second yellow card in the 89th minute, but the decision was the correct one in an otherwise well-managed affair.

Fabian Hurzeler's side enjoyed a strong first half, in which they could have had three of four goals if not for an outstanding performance from goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

However, Hull had chances of their own, mostly in the second half, before Ollie McBurnie scored the first goal in the 92nd minute to send the home crowd wild, before adding a second just minute later.

While Bankes did not make any massive errors, both sides will claim they should have had decisions go their way which could have swung the eventual result.

The game's biggest controversy came shortly before half-time, when Hull City thought they should have had a penalty when Mohamed-Ali Cho was pulled in the box.

After the ball broke loose from a corner, the forward turned to keep the move alive, and Brighton defender Joao Costinha had a handfull of his shirt.

Had Cho gone to ground, there is a real chance Hull could have been awarded a penalty which would have given them the opportunity to go 1-0 up at home.

However, VAR reviewed the situation, and despite replays shoing a clear pull from the Brighton man, they decided no further action was needed.

Just minutes following Hull's loud calls for a penalty, Brighton had claims of their own, after Pascal Gross went to ground on the edge of the six-yard box.

The midfielder would have had a tap-in to put his side ahead shortly before the break if he had not been tripped by the Hull City defender.

After Gross missed out, the ball fell to Diego Gomez at the back post, but his effort was pushed wide by the ankle of Tzolakis in what was another fine save from the keeper.

However, that was not enough to appease Gross, who was left raging by the decision not to award a penalty which, again, was checked and cleared by VAR.

Luka Vuskovic might consider himself lucky to have remained on the pitch for the full match after numerous encounters with Hull striker, and eventual match-winner, McBurnie.

The Croatia international was given a yellow card in the 34th minute after he petulantly kicked the ball away, and was walking a tightrope ever since.

However, he managed to get away with five fouls, and with his yellow card having come as a result of delaying the restart, he went without punishment for all five.

It may have been harsh to see Vuskovic sent off for any of the individual indiscretions, but as the fouls racked up, it was a surprise not to see him sanctioned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

24 hours on from West Ham’s  tepid point against the bottom side in the league and whilst the justified criticism is flying around, there are definitely positives to pull out of a fixture in which West Ham dominated all the important statistics save the most important one: The points tally at the final whistle.

Sadly, again the Hammers have lost ground on the leaders and now sit eight points adrift. And yet, from Scott Parker’s comments, there are definite signs that he’s learned from at least some of the mistakes made by his predecessor. Reversing Nuno’s decision to cast out Edson Alvarez from the senior team proved a massive success.. Who knew.

Yesterday’s re-integration of ‘El Machin’ into the starting line up was his first league appearance in a West Ham shirt since May 2025.

This was an Alvarez playing more like his first season as a Hammer.

The Mexican clearly cares: He was in tears before kick off, so tough has his time in the football wilderness been.

It has been revealed that having been such a critic of him during his card-strewn Lopetegui era, credit where it is due. Edson Alvarez was, indeed, excellent yesterday and it is a testimony to his professionalism that he played a full ninety after not playing competitive football since August.

Two weeks’ work during the international break had accounted for very little as Preston withstood everything the Hammers and their almost 60,000 fans had to throw at their lowly opponents.

And therein lies the problem. Having surrendered the small, intimidating, sometimes downright hostile atmosphere of Upton Park back in 2016, the distance from the pitch and the wide open spaces of the Olympic Stadium are about as intimidating as a day out at London Zoo for our opponents and their fans who continue to pour scorn on the venue.

According to recent reports, it just doesn’t strike fear into opponents as it should. Even when we score.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium – as our opponents are finding out.

Preston fan Tm Mercer, writing in the Lancashire Evening Post, makes it abundantly clear that there was no noticeable crowd reaction to lift the home side, as there should have been once Mavropanos restored parity:.

“Aside from play-off finals, I’m pretty certain it is the first time I’ve been in a stadium for a league match with 60,000-plus through the gate.

Yet, when they equalised, it did not feel like the roar of that many people in such a cavernous ground. Give me somewhere like Gigg Lane, stood in their paddock pitch side, any day!”.

For the uninitiated, Gigg Lane is the home of Bury FC with a capacity of around…..12,000.

Nobody is suggesting the Hammers fans were silent. The cursèd accoustics from the soulless bowl and sheer distance from the pitch play right into opponents’ hands. And, ten years after moving in, it’s going to take a lot more than some safe standing and a couple of family zones to fix it.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's fresh full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly.

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo.

They are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The newly introduced national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

According to recent reports, his form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

Recent findings suggest that but it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

Industry observers note that the attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

Industry observers note that he had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

He was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he mentioned: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'.

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the big-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut.

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside.

'The media made me substantial, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the looks, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

Sources indicate that 'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'.

He was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he announced himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season.

Industry observers note that 'Today is a dream come true,' he stated after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

Industry observers note that after 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of newly introduced manager Jorge Jesus.

Recent findings suggest that when pressed if he was the newly introduced permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he said.

Then he added: 'We know it's a major, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'.

In a recent development, it remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

Manchester United may have reason to complaint after Leny Yoro was sent off just minutes into their defeat against Liverpool.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that initially he thought the decision was "clear" and could not be argued with.

However, after reviewing upcoming angles and footage emerging from Anfield, the refereeing expert changed his mind, insisting the decision was more subjective than it seemed.

The resulting free kick was slammed home by Dominik Szoboszlai to put his side ahead early in the game, before Florian Wirtz put the hosts two in front three minutes later.

Man United were then put to the sword in the second half as Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz both found the net to ensure all three points came in a 4-0 win for Liverpool.

Pochettino has a lot of work to do to turn around his side's dismal start to the season, with Man United still trapped inside the Premier League's relegation zone.

Referee Sam Barrott was forced into an early decision at Anfield as he swiftly brandished the red card, sending Yoro down the tunnell, and the call was confirmed by VAR.

Some, likely including Pochettino, have since pointed to the fact that Isak's touch had sent the ball well in front of him, and he was unlikely to get a shot off from there.

That has led to questions about the law, which does suggest that VAR must assess whether the attacking player was likely to keep hold of the ball.

However, the final decision was that Yoro had denied Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity and the defender was shown a straight red card.

Barrott has been praised for his quick decision-making in a high-pressure scenario, especially so early in the game, as he immediately reached to his pocket to brandish the card.

However, VAR does have the benefit of seeing immediate replays, and questions have since been asked about whether Barrott should have been sent to the monitor.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett explained: "That was a clear foul by Yoro, just outside his penalty area, which clearly denies a goal-scoring opportunity.

According to recent reports, "Referee Barrott rightly, without hesitation, produced the red card out of his left-hand pocket. Clear denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

"Very good piece of officiating, the referee was in a great position and without hesitation made the correct call. Manchester United can have no complaints.".

However, he later made a U-turn, as he explained: "The criteria for DOGSO is as follows: The following must be considered; the distance between the offence and the goal, the general direction of play, and likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball.

"When you review the replays, which VAR does, what was the likihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball? That is where there is an element of doubt. A subjective call.".

Those doubts have been made clear by Man United fans in the wake of the decision, and by Pochettino on the sidelines, but the decision seemed straightforward in the moment.

Liverpool will be delighted with the majority of their star players following a dominant 3-0 win against Manchester United.

The Reds eased to a comfortable victory at Anfield, and ruined Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Man United manager despite their pre-game optimism.

After Leny Yoro was sent off just eight minutes into the clash, and Dominik Szoboszlai put his side ahead from the resulting free-kick, before Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 minutes later.

That strong start gave them a comfortable platform to build on before goals from Rio Ngunoha and Victor Munoz, and while the 4-0 final score was not the 7-0 demolition we saw in 2023, it was arguably just as comfortable for them.

Liverpool's defensive players and goalkeeper had very little to do throughout, but handled their responsibilities well when asked.

The midfield and attack, however, were allowed to shine and display their talents in what was finally a statement win for Andoni Iraola at Anfield, where they have otherwise struggled.

Wirtz has been heavily criticised during his time at Liverpool, with a lofty price tag and a lack of consistency leading to constant jibes about his performances.

However, he has shown a remarkable turn of form of late, and thrived under Liverpool legend Jurgen Klopp in the most recent international break with Germany.

He seems to have returned to Anfield a latest man, as he scored the second goal of the game and set up the fourth, while he completed ten key passes, created four major chances and completed 100 per cent of his dribbles.

Outside of the statistics, however, his constant energy and running in behiind posed a threat, while his movement and quick-thinking caused Man United no end of trouble.

While there have been questions asked of his continued involvement since his move in 2025, the midfielder showed today he can be worth every penny of that £116million.

Bradley Barcola looked electric on the wing whenever he got the ball, got into some great positions and was a constant threat for the fresh-look Man United back line.

His pace and close control made him a dangerous asset for the Reds, but ultimately his end product let him down, as has been the story of his Liverpool career so far.

In a recent development, speaking live on Sky Sports, Jamie Carragher insisted Barcola "lets himself down" with his end product after consistently failing to provide goals and assists. He later labeled him "unconvincing".

Barcola was later booked for a late challenge on the edge of the Man United area, capping off what was a disappointing display for the £123million man.

Despite eventually picking up an assist when he set up Rio Ngumoha's finish, the France international could and should have left Anfield with four or five contributions.

The disparity between the two clubs is significant at the moment, even though Wyness believes that the 49ers’ looks are beginning to work at Ibrox.

Aberdeen’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Pittodrie between 2000 and 2004 and now runs a consultancy business advising elite clubs – believes that Rangers fans shouldn’t be concerned over the 49ers’ ability to fund both clubs long-term.

The Scottish businessman sees their push for a new investment as a move to help realise their ambitions, rather than an indication that they are struggling to help the clubs progress.

In a recent development, “Now, I think Rangers should be very happy having the 49ers still as owners there. And I think they're making progress.

According to recent reports, “But, I wouldn't be concerned about Leeds getting extra investment because I think Rangers can get that extra investment if they put forward the right case. But they've got to show that they're disciplined, that things are happening in the right way.

In a recent development, “I think they’ll be the conversations that are going on. They're starting to show signs of doing things correctly and getting the right structure together. So no, I wouldn't be concerned in the slightest if I was a Rangers fan. I think it's just good, prudent management from the 49ers.”.

Roy Keane was left furious following Manchester United's heavy defeat against Liverpool and made his anger very clear.

The former Red Devils midfielder, and no-nonsense pundit, savaged the current crop of players as well as his fellow pundit Gary Neville in the wake of the 4-0 defeat.

Mauricio Pochettino's side fell 2-0 down just 13 minutes into the game, after Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz found the net following an early red card for Leny Yoro.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz doubled the scoreline in the second half, and Liverpool could have had more, having created countless chances to put their rivals away.

There were echoes of the 7-0 win Liverpool recorded against Man United in 2023, and yet, the fans applauded the players off the pitch and pundits have begun making excuses.

Keane, however, was not in a mood to tolerate excuses and he demanded the players take responsibility and the pundits, including Gary Neville, assess their priorities.

Yoro's red card is largely being pinned as the reason for Man United's defeat, having ripped up any intends they had heading into what was always set to be a tough game.

However, Keane has insisted that cannot be the only reason for the defeat, as he questioned how teams have coped in the past after going down to ten men early in the game.

While the 4-0 scoreline did flatter Man United, that should be treated as a major concern rather than a positive to take from the game, and Keane has made his feelings clear.

Speaking live on Sky Sports, he ranted: "If I hear that one more time from the lads on commentary and in the studio, '4-0 is not too bad, we were down to ten men', has a team never got a result before with ten men?

Industry observers note that "I thought they were so bad. Neville, who's played for Man United hundreds of times, saying he's okay with 4-0? Are you telling me they couldn't have done better?

Recent findings suggest that "At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality. I can't believe what I'm hearing from people who've played for the club.

According to recent reports, "The fans are applauding the players. Applauding what? Applauding rubbish.

"This team, two years ago, finished 15th and the last year or two we're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers, when do the players take responsibility?

"Liverpool probably should've scored eight or nine, and everyone's coming off the pitch saying 'four's not too bad', I feel like swearing.".

Despite the result and Keane's rant, there can be no doubt that the biggest talking point will centre around Yoro's red card and the impact it had on the game.

While it should not be used as an excuse for their dismal performance, it certainly weakened the side, and Liverpool took full advantage in the minutes that followed.

However, former PGMOL chief Keith Hackett told Football Insider that Man United may have reason to complain after analysing footage of Yoro's dismissal.

While referee Sam Barrott made a quick decision to brandish a red card for denying a goalscoring opportunity, replays suggested it may not have met all of the criteria.

Questions have been asked about whether Alexander Isak would have got to the ball, and as a result, the subjective decision is bound to cause debates.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Koni De Winter spoke at an event at the AC Milan store today, and he covered numerous topics with a lot of openness.
  • Recent findings suggest that this season, De Winter has found himself in a new, key light.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Koni De Winter spoke at an event at the AC Milan store today, and he covered numerous topics with a lot of openness.

Recent findings suggest that this season, De Winter has found himself in a new, key light. Matteo Gabbia spent most of pre-season in the middle of the back three, but injuries have prevented him from playing much of a role in the campaign.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, it’s an unfortunate shame and there may have been some worries about De Winter taking on this role. However, he’s taken the opportunity in his stride, looking every part a starter in Ruben Amorim’s defence.

In a recent development, rumours about a fresh defender arriving will persist, so it’ll be interesting to see what happens with his minutes from January onwards. However, he’s created something of a headache, but it’s a good one to have.

Speaking to SportMediaset on the sidelines of the Meet&Greet at the Milan Store in San Babila, via MilanNews, De Winter looked at the rise in his playing time, Amorim’s closeness to the group and much more.

In a recent development, you also took over at Reggio Emilia when Gabbia was unfortunately injured. You’re practically always there; what does that mean to you?

“I’m playing a lot, it’s great to be playing. We’re playing a lot, and these days you train more on taking care of your body, keeping healthy, and right now I’m doing that more, but it’s great to be playing a lot of games. Playing a lot of games for Milan, and it’s even better to win games.”.

According to recent reports, it’s all great, but it wasn’t a given: you’ve earned this place as leader. Do you now feel like a leader of this AC Milan?

“I feel good at this Milan club, and as I always say, I try to give what I can. It’s also true that I might have a more important position this year. That might be true, but I always try to do my part, give my all, and help my teammates.”.

It’s clear, evident, that Amorim holds you in high regard, but what is Amorim like? An adjective.

“I’d say he’s very human. He’s one of us, he laughs, he has fun, but when he has to be serious, he’s serious. He lives with the group, the group feels close to him, and I think that gives the players a good feeling. It’s nice to work for him and with him.”.

Is it true that he got very angry after the defeat against Ferencvaros?

“Yes, but I think the whole group felt that we had played a very poor game, so, as I saw it, my teammates saw it too.”.

It has been revealed that are Ferencvaros and Bologna two games you’re ready to say “never again” to? Will Frosinone be a different team?

“Yes, exactly, as I mentioned, we are very confident, but sometimes even too much so, and then all matches are difficult against whoever we play against, and we have to understand this rapidly and we can’t make the same mistakes.”.

Among the various critics, it’s said that this AC Milan team has enormous potential, but there are too many ups and downs. Does it need more consistency?

Recent findings suggest that “Yes, I think it hurts even more when we lose because we know we can do well, we can win every game. So yes, when we really lose, in the locker room you feel like we’ve let ourselves down first and then everyone else.”.

You recently became the father of a beautiful baby girl. What are your nights like as a dad?

“At night, I’m fine. My girlfriend is working really hard, so it’s a lot for me. I mean, I get up sometimes, but it’s much quieter. I think it’s harder for her.”.

And how much has life changed with the arrival of a daughter?

According to recent reports, “It’s changed a lot, I mean, I don’t know how to explain it. When you’re at work, you think about your daughter, you want to come home earlier, you want to hold her, you want her – I mean, you have more beautiful moments – but it’s hard to explain. I don’t know how to explain it.”.

You were also used as a full-back, but now you only play as a centre-back….

“Good, good, because I also consider myself a centre-back, but it’s true that I can also play full-back. It’s something I can do, but it’s not my favourite position. But yes, it’s true that I’ve played a few games there in the past, but I’m happy playing as a centre back and I’m happy that the coach sees that too.”.

According to recent reports, “I mean, crazy in a good way, yes. He likes to have fun, he likes to dance, he likes to talk, so he’s a bright spot, as they say, for the locker room, yes.”.

It has been revealed that “Well, that’s a good question. Yes, I miss her. I thought about it even when the little girl was born: I also want to score a goal, I mean, dedicate a goal to her, so I miss her, yes.”.

How do you concentrate when you’re in the hotel retreat? How do you focus in the hours leading up to kick-off?

Industry observers note that “It’s become a routine now, so I always do the same things. You’re in the hotel, you take a shower, you play a little video game or you’re on your phone, so now I don’t even think about it, it’s really become a routine.”.

What does Maignan ask of you, defenders?

“He claims to stay focused on the game because, as we know, one moment can change the game and at Milan it can also change a season, so it’s very important not to underestimate every moment and always stay focused.

It seems to me that there is a great understanding between you and Strahinja Pavlovic even off the pitch….

“Yes, it’s true, he and I have a good relationship; we met last year. Then when you see him you might not think, I mean, I didn’t think he would be such a great friend, but we got along really well both on and off the pitch, it’s really nice to spend time with him.”.

Our 007s at Milanello tell us about some great ping pong matches between you and Pavlovic. Who’s the better player?

In a recent development, “This is difficult, but he started at a much higher level than me. But now I’ve improved a lot, although I have to say he’s even stronger. But yes, every day we start with a game of ping pong and then we start working.”.

Would you like your daughter to play soccer in the future? Are you planning a second child? Would you like to have a son who plays soccer?

It has been revealed that “I want her to do what she wants, where she feels good, where she doesn’t feel pressured, and where she can express herself best. And then, going back to ping pong, I think there’s some video; maybe we can see me beat her.”.

#61000. Latest Update: What it's really like to kill a fellow athlete - and the terrible grief 'you carry for the rest of your life': The cursed band of haunted sportsmen reveal the nightmares that never leave them

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3880 w)
📖 Baca

Latest Update: What it's really like to kill a fellow athlete - and the terrible grief 'you carry for the rest of your life': The cursed band of haunted sportsmen reveal the nightmares that never leave them

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and Upcoming South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.
  • Australian sport was still in shock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.

Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and Upcoming South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.

Australian sport was still in shock. A few months earlier, Australia's Test opener, Phillip Hughes, had died after he was struck on the side of his neck by a short ball from a young bowler called Sean Abbott in a game between New South Wales and South Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Hughes was treated at the ground for 40 minutes and then taken by ambulance to St Vincent's Hospital in nearby Darlinghurst in a critical condition. 'Feeling for Phil Hughes after being hit,' former Australia Test cricketer Dean Jones wrote on Twitter. 'He is not in a good way! Stay strong Sean Abbott. Not your fault, young man.'.

The impact of the ball had compressed a vein in Hughes' neck and when it split, it caused a catastrophic bleed on the brain. Hughes had emergency surgery and was placed in an induced coma. He never regained consciousness and passed away two days later.

Hughes was a popular, talented, gutsy cricketer with three Test centuries already under his belt. A small guy with the heart of a lion. He was 25 years old. Cricket mourned a terrible tragedy – some called it the sport's saddest day and the agony of Hughes' family was hard to bear. But there was something else. There was an awareness that two tragedies were playing out in front of us.

Sources indicate that hughes was lost but the man who had bowled the delivery that felled him had been left behind, desolate and distraught. Many thought Sean Abbott, who was 22, would never play cricket again. That he would not be able to find the strength. But that was why I had flown to Tasmania. Because Abbott had found the strength.

Phil Hughes was the golden boy of Australian cricket in 2014, with three Test centuries already to his name, when he was hit by a ball bowled by Sean Abbott and died.

Abbott visiting the Sydney hospital where Hughes was in a coma that he would never wake from, having suffered a catastrophic bleed on the brain.

That February afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I sat among a smattering of spectators who watched Abbott walk to the top of his mark. His team-mates shouted encouragement to him. They were willing him on with everything they had and Abbott bowled his heart out.

Sources indicate that 'Beautifully bowled, Abbo,' one of the NSW fielders shouted after one ball to former Test opener Ed Cowan. 'That's a beauty, Seanie,' another yelled after the fifth ball of his first over, when Cowan jerked his head out of the way of a short delivery so fast he fell over. Only one wicket fell that afternoon. Abbott took it.

It was one of the bravest sporting performances I have ever witnessed. Because even though cricket had voiced its support for Abbott, the sport could not protect him from his thoughts and from the knowledge he had become one of a cursed band of sportsmen who have unwittingly caused the death of an opponent during a contest.

Sometimes, tragedy in sport is not just the tragedy of the player who dies; it is the tragedy of the opponent who must live the nightmare of what he has done over and over again in his mind. To those that it has befallen, they say it is a grief that never leaves them.

That grief, that sense of a double tragedy, was brought sharply back into focus earlier this month when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono. The accident happened in the final minutes of a game in Spain's Segunda Division, when Owono hurtled out of his goal and collided with De Miguel in the centre circle. He was shown a red card for the foul.

There was an outpouring of grief for De Miguel. I was among those who observed a minute's silence for him before the Barcelona-Aston Villa Champions League tie at the Nou Camp the next evening. Tributes continue to be paid to him. Owono, meanwhile, has become a pariah. It is noted that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

Sources indicate that owono does not appear to have had the same sympathy extended to him that Abbott benefited from. His challenge on De Miguel, a striker who had had a peripatetic career in Spain's lower leagues, was reckless and cavalier. For him, the struggle with guilt and responsibility and public judgment is only just beginning.

FC Andorra will play their first home game since the tragedy against Leganes on Friday night but when they run out at the Encamp Stadium, a neat little ground beside a babbling river, the Valira d'Orient, and in the shadow of the mountains that make Andorra such a popular ski resort, Owono will not be there.

Earlier this month Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

Owono has become a pariah. It is said that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

The goalkeeper, who has 47 caps for Equatorial Guinea, was given the maximum sentence of a 12-match ban by the Spanish Football Federation.

Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera suggested Owono's ban 'might feel light' to all those mourning the striker, who was 30 years old, while FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique, the former Barcelona and Spain centre back, mentioned the maximum sanction 'puts him (Owono) in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened'.

According to recent reports, no one knows whether Owono will feel able to return to football when his ban ends. Footage circulated of him in an on-field argument moments before the clash with De Miguel, and it was used to suggest that he was in an unstable state of mind.

It has been revealed that some have pressed for him to be charged with manslaughter. His Instagram account was deactivated after it was deluged with abuse, including messages which branded him 'a murderer'. It has been reported that his brother, who is also a footballer, has been the victim of abuse because of his association with Owono.

In a recent development, owono has only communicated through a statement released by his club. 'These are the most difficult days of my life,' he wrote. 'I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.'.

According to recent reports, I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies. His brother, Dermot, took his own life. University of North Carolina academic John M Silva III argued that aggression in sport is defined in two categories: hostile aggression and instrumental aggression.
